title: Long Short-Term Memory
what: Introduces the LSTM cell, which mitigates vanishing gradients in recurrent networks.
how: Gated memory cells with a constant error carousel; trained with truncated backpropagation through time.
results: Learns dependencies over 1,000+ time steps where earlier RNNs fail.
usage: Background section — the standard recurrent baseline for forecasting experiments.

title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
what: Proposes the RNN encoder-decoder and the gated recurrent unit (GRU).
how: Two RNNs (encoder, decoder) trained jointly; the GRU uses reset and update gates.
results: Improves phrase-based translation scores; the GRU becomes a lighter alternative to the LSTM.
usage: Methods section — justify the GRU as a cheaper recurrent baseline.

title: Attention Is All You Need
what: Introduces the Transformer, built entirely on self-attention.
how: Multi-head scaled dot-product attention with positional encodings; no recurrence.
results: State-of-the-art translation quality with much faster training than RNNs.
usage: Background section — origin of attention-based forecasting models.

title: Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting
what: Adapts the Transformer to long-horizon time-series forecasting.
how: ProbSparse self-attention, self-attention distilling, and a generative-style decoder.
results: Outperforms LSTM and vanilla Transformer baselines on long-horizon benchmarks.
usage: Related work — strongest attention-based forecasting baseline to compare against.

title: Human-Level Control through Deep Reinforcement Learning
what: The Deep Q-Network (DQN) learns control policies directly from high-dimensional input.
how: Q-learning with a convolutional network, experience replay, and a target network.
results: Human-level performance on 29 of 49 Atari games with a single architecture.
usage: Methods section — reference RL algorithm for turning forecasts into decisions.
